verbs.nuance_ko: 돈이나 귀중한 것을 억지로 혹은 마지못해 넘겨줄 때 생생한 느낌을 살려 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: I had to fork over a lot of money to fix my broken car.
verbs.my_line: I had to fork over extra cash for express shipping last week.

verbs.nuance_ko: 돈이나 자원이 넉넉하지 않아 겨우 생활을 유지할 때 원어민들이 입버릇처럼 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: She barely scraped by on her small salary during her first year in the city.
verbs.my_line: I barely scraped by financially before I got my current job.

verbs.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 만난 사람과 밀린 이야기를 나누거나 안부를 물을 때 원어민들이 가장 즐겨 쓰는 자연스러운 표현입니다.
verbs.example: We should grab a cup of coffee this weekend and catch up on everything.
verbs.my_line: I am planning to catch up with my old college friend this Friday night.

verbs.nuance_ko: 바쁜 하루나 한 주를 보낸 뒤 서서히 휴식 상태로 들어가며 긴장을 풀 때 주로 사용합니다.
verbs.example: I usually listen to some soft acoustic music to wind down after work.
verbs.my_line: I love to watch a funny movie to wind down after a long stressful day.

verbs.nuance_ko: 복잡한 문제나 혼란스러운 상황을 깔끔하게 정리하고 해결할 때 원어민들이 가장 즐겨 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: We need to sort out this billing error before the end of the day.
verbs.my_line: I had a scheduling conflict this week, but thankfully I managed to sort it out.

verbs.nuance_ko: 계획을 진행하던 중 예상치 못한 난관이나 문제를 우연히 맞닥뜨렸을 때 자연스럽게 사용할 수 있습니다.
verbs.example: The development team ran into a major technical issue during the software update.
verbs.my_line: I ran into a few unexpected problems while working on my project yesterday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 단순히 떠나는 것보다 집이나 사무실에서 목적지로 나서는 활기찬 뉘앙스를 줍니다.
verbs.example: I always head out a bit early to avoid the heavy morning traffic.
verbs.my_line: I usually head out for work around 8 AM to beat the rush hour.

verbs.meaning_ko: (교통 등으로) 지연되다, 꼼짝 못 하게 하다
verbs.nuance_ko: 예상치 못한 문제나 교통 체증 때문에 멈춰 서 있을 때 원어민들이 입버릇처럼 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: Bad weather on the highway can seriously hold up your daily commute.
verbs.my_line: My train got delayed today, and that really held up my morning schedule.

verbs.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 물리적으로 출발했던 장소로 되돌아갈 때 'return'보다 훨씬 자연스럽게 쓰입니다.
verbs.example: After a long and tiring day at the office, I usually head back home.
verbs.my_line: I usually head back home right after finishing my last meeting every Tuesday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 교통체증이나 예상치 못한 상황으로 인해 갇히거나 정체될 때 감정을 실어 생생하게 표현하기 좋습니다.
verbs.example: Unfortunately, my bus got stuck in heavy morning traffic on the highway.
verbs.my_line: Sometimes I get stuck in heavy traffic on my way to work.

verbs.nuance_ko: 과도한 일이나 스트레스로 인해 에너지가 완전히 바닥났을 때 일상적으로 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: If you work too many hours without a break, you will quickly burn out.
verbs.my_line: I sometimes worry that I might burn out if I take on too many projects.

verbs.nuance_ko: 흥분하거나 화가 난 상태를 가라앉힐 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: Take a deep breath and try to calm down before you make a decision.
verbs.my_line: I usually listen to soft acoustic music to calm down after a stressful day.

verbs.nuance_ko: 단순히 떠나는 것보다 집이나 사무실 같은 실내 공간에서 목적지를 향해 문을 나서며 이동을 시작할 때 훨씬 자연스럽습니다.
verbs.example: I usually head out around seven thirty to avoid the heavy morning rush hour traffic.
verbs.my_line: I had to head out a bit earlier today because the subway was extremely crowded.

verbs.nuance_ko: 계획 없이 길이나 대중교통 안에서 우연히 아는 사람을 만났을 때 쓰는 아주 생동감 있는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: I was surprised to run into my old college roommate on the morning train yesterday.
verbs.my_line: I hope I do not run into my annoying boss on my way to the office.

verbs.nuance_ko: 공식적인 회의 전이나 결정을 내리기 전에 상대방에게 아이디어를 가볍게 공유하고 반응을 볼 때 원어민들이 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: Let me run this new schedule idea by my manager before we finalize it.
verbs.my_line: I need to run my project proposal by my team leader this afternoon.

verbs.nuance_ko: 누군가 어려움을 겪고 있거나 문제가 생겼을 때 자원해서 도움을 주거나 상황을 수습하기 위해 나설 때 사용합니다.
verbs.example: My colleague had to step in and help me finish the presentation on time.
verbs.my_line: I had to step in when our team faced an unexpected technical issue yesterday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 우리 몸이 감기나 피로 같은 공격적인 요소를 적극적으로 막아낼 때 원어민들이 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: I drink plenty of warm lemon water to fight off a bad cold.
verbs.my_line: I am trying to fight off a mild cold since the weather got colder.

verbs.nuance_ko: 에너지가 완전히 고갈되어 지쳐버린 상태를 시각적으로 잘 나타내 주는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: Running a marathon without proper training will completely wear your body out.
verbs.my_line: My heavy workload at the office usually wears me out by Thursday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 격식 없는 일상 회화에서 주로 사용하며, 대상을 사이에 넣을 수 있는 분리형 동사입니다.
verbs.example: We had to put off our team meeting until Thursday morning due to traffic.
verbs.my_line: I had to put off my dentist appointment this week because of extra work.

verbs.nuance_ko: 회의, 업무, 하루 일과 등을 최종적으로 깔끔하게 끝마칠 때 원어민들이 가장 즐겨 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: Let's try to wrap up this project before the weekend arrives without fail.
verbs.my_line: I usually try to wrap up all my important tasks by four o'clock every day.

verbs.nuance_ko: 의견이나 주장을 데이터나 사실로 뒷받침할 때 원어민들이 아주 즐겨 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: You need to back up your proposal with solid market data before presenting.
verbs.my_line: I always try to back up my weekly reports with actual sales numbers.

verbs.nuance_ko: 필요할 때 자원해서 나서거나 기존의 노력이나 속도를 더 끌어올릴 때 사용합니다.
verbs.example: We need to step up our marketing efforts to reach the quarterly targets.
verbs.my_line: I had to step up my game this week because of the sudden project deadline.

verbs.nuance_ko: 매우 놀라거나 당황해서 감정이 통제되지 않을 때 쓰는 일상적인 표현입니다.
verbs.example: I always freak out whenever I have to give a sudden presentation.
verbs.my_line: I tend to freak out when my computer suddenly freezes during work.

verbs.nuance_ko: 기분이 안 좋은 사람에게 기운을 북돋아 주거나 스스로 기분을 풀 때 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: My friends tried to cheer me up with some delicious spicy food.
verbs.my_line: I usually listen to upbeat music to cheer myself up on busy mornings.

verbs.nuance_ko: 단순히 피곤한 것을 넘어 과로나 스트레스로 심신이 완전히 지쳐 더 이상 에너지가 없을 때 주로 씁니다.
verbs.example: If you work too many overtime hours this week, you will quickly burn out.
verbs.my_line: I felt like I was going to burn out by Wednesday because of heavy workloads.

verbs.nuance_ko: 갑작스러운 일에 지나치게 놀라거나 당황해서 어쩔 줄 모르는 감정을 생생하게 표현할 때 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: I always freak out when my computer crashes right before an important deadline.
verbs.my_line: I nearly freaked out when my boss asked me to present without any preparation.

verbs.nuance_ko: 감기나 피로 같은 부정적인 요소를 적극적으로 물리칠 때 원어민들이 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: I am trying to fight off a bad cold before the big presentation.
verbs.my_line: I tried to fight off my afternoon fatigue by drinking a strong coffee.

verbs.nuance_ko: 에너지를 완전히 소모하여 녹초가 만들거나 물건이 닳아 없어질 때 주로 사용합니다.
verbs.example: Intensive morning workouts usually wear me out for the rest of the day.
verbs.my_line: My heavy workload last week completely wore me out by Friday night.

verbs.nuance_ko: 다림질하듯 작은 마찰이나 세부 사항을 매끄럽게 정리할 때 주로 씁니다.
verbs.example: We need to iron out a few final details before signing the contract.
verbs.my_line: I had to iron out a schedule conflict with my client this morning.

verbs.nuance_ko: 예상치 못한 문제나 장애물을 우연히 마주쳤을 때 자연스럽게 사용합니다.
verbs.example: The development team ran into a serious bug while testing the new app.
verbs.my_line: I ran into some unexpected trouble while trying to finish my report yesterday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 의도치 않게 스르륵 잠에 빠져들 때 주로 쓰며, 낮 시간이나 지루한 상황에서 흔히 씁니다.
verbs.example: I always tend to doze off during long afternoon meetings at work.
verbs.my_line: I almost doze off on the subway because I stayed up late studying.

verbs.nuance_ko: 피곤하거나 우울하던 사람이 커피나 좋은 소식 덕분에 활기를 되찾을 때 자연스럽습니다.
verbs.example: Drinking a large iced coffee usually helps me perk up in the morning.
verbs.my_line: I usually perk up right after I drink my morning coffee.

verbs.nuance_ko: 주로 물건이나 시간, 에너지가 완전히 소진되어 더 이상 없을 때 자연스럽게 씁니다.
verbs.example: We need to go to the grocery store because the milk has run out.
verbs.my_line: I realized my coffee had run out right before my morning meeting started.

verbs.nuance_ko: 제안이나 초대 등을 정중하게 거절하거나 볼륨을 줄일 때 일상적으로 아주 많이 사용합니다.
verbs.example: She decided to turn down the job offer because the commute was too long.
verbs.my_line: I had to turn down a dinner invitation last night because I was too tired.

verbs.nuance_ko: 이미 예정된 행사나 회의를 더 이상 진행하지 않기로 결정할 때 원어민들이 'cancel' 대신 훨씬 더 자주 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: We had to call off the weekly marketing meeting because the manager was sick.
verbs.my_line: I had to call off my dentist appointment this morning due to an urgent task.

verbs.nuance_ko: 회의나 발표 전에 준비된 내용을 빠르게 점검하거나 리허설할 때 주로 사용하는 자연스러운 표현입니다.
verbs.example: Let's quickly run through the slide deck before the client presentation starts.
verbs.my_line: I need to run through my presentation notes one more time before our 1:1 call.

verbs.nuance_ko: 계획이나 일상 업무를 진행하다가 예상치 못한 장애물이나 문제를 만났을 때 자연스럽게 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: We might run into some unexpected technical issues during the live online presentation.
verbs.my_line: I ran into a minor problem with my computer while working from home this morning.

verbs.nuance_ko: 복잡한 상황이나 문제를 깊이 생각하여 답을 찾아내거나 이해했을 때 주로 사용하는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: It took me a few hours to figure out why the software was crashing.
verbs.my_line: I need to figure out how to manage my busy schedule more effectively this week.

verbs.nuance_ko: 확정되지 않은 일정을 연필로 적어두듯 유연하게 잡을 때 원어민들이 자주 씁니다.
verbs.example: Let's pencil in our meeting for next Thursday morning and confirm later.
verbs.my_line: Can we pencil in our next conversation class for this coming Friday afternoon?

verbs.nuance_ko: 격식 있는 단어 대신 일상이나 업무에서 일정을 연기할 때 가장 입에 붙는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: We had to push back the project deadline because of unexpected technical issues.
verbs.my_line: I might need to push back my schedule because my meeting is running long.

verbs.nuance_ko: 감기 같은 질병이나 피로가 몸에 침투하지 못하게 저항할 때 자연스럽게 씁니다.
verbs.example: I drank plenty of warm lemon tea to fight off the mild cold.
verbs.my_line: I tried to fight off my afternoon fatigue by drinking a large iced americano.

verbs.nuance_ko: 과도한 업무나 스트레스로 인해 완전히 에너지가 바닥나 더 이상 일할 수 없는 상태를 뜻합니다.
verbs.example: Workers often burn out quickly when they take on too many projects simultaneously.
verbs.my_line: I need to balance my workload carefully this week so I do not burn out.

verbs.nuance_ko: 문제가 생겼을 때 임시로라도 빠르게 수습하거나 관계를 회복할 때 주로 사용합니다.
verbs.example: We need to patch up the critical bug in the software before the update.
verbs.my_line: I had to patch up a major scheduling conflict with my team yesterday.

verbs.nuance_ko: 단서를 쫓아 숨겨져 있거나 찾기 힘든 사람이나 물건을 결국 찾아낼 때 씁니다.
verbs.example: It took me hours to track down the missing invoice in our system.
verbs.my_line: I spent the entire morning trying to track down the source of this error.

verbs.nuance_ko: 운전 중 길가에 안전하게 차를 멈출 때 주로 쓰는 표현입니다.
verbs.example: The police officer told me to pull over because of a flat tire.
verbs.my_line: I had to pull over to check my navigation system during my commute this morning.

verbs.nuance_ko: 시간이나 스케줄이 계획보다 지체되고 있을 때 자연스럽게 쓰입니다.
verbs.example: We are running behind schedule due to heavy traffic on the highway.
verbs.my_line: I was running behind this morning because my train arrived much later than usual.
